Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister inaugurates new state-of-the-art building of Income Tax Department 'Aayakar Sindhu' at Nariman Point, Mumbai
articles.full_content:
Smt. Sitharaman urges Income Tax Officers to exercise their authority with empathy, sensitivity and a spirit of public service, ensuring that governance remains citizen-centric
: Mumbai, July 26, 2026
The Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurated ‘Aayakar Sindhu’, the new state-of-the-art office complex of the Income Tax Department at Nariman Point, Mumbai, and dedicated it to the service of the nation.
Speaking on the occasion which falls on Kargil Vijay Diwas, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman first paid heartfelt tributes to the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the 1999 Kargil War. Emphasising the values of patriotism and public service, she said, "We will ensure every institution of the Republic remains worthy of their sacrifice."
Referring to the newly inaugurated Income Tax Department office, "Aayakar Sindhu", located at Nariman Point, Mumbai, Smt. Sitharaman noted that the locality is named after noted freedom fighter Khurshed Framji Nariman. She urged officers of the Income Tax Department to serve the nation with integrity and dedication as a tribute to the soldiers and freedom fighters who devoted their lives to the country.
Addressing the Income Tax officers, the Finance Minister observed that they are privileged to serve the nation in a highly sensitive role that demands the highest standards of honesty, professionalism and integrity.
Explaining the significance of the name "Aayakar Sindhu", Smt. Sitharaman said it aptly reflects the role of the Income Tax Department. Just as the ocean (Sindhu) receives water from countless rivers, the Department mobilises tax revenues from taxpayers across the country and channels them into the Consolidated Fund of India, from where resources are utilised for nation-building and public welfare.
Smt. Sitharaman spoke about the challenges encountered in clearances and removing encroachments before the construction of Aayakar Sindhu. Stating this, the Finance Minister urged officers to reflect on the difficulties often faced by ordinary citizens in resolving their day-to-day issues. She called upon them to exercise their authority with empathy, sensitivity and a spirit of public service, ensuring that governance remains citizen-centric.
Smt. Sitharaman also assured Income Tax officials that the Government is committed to improving office infrastructure and residential accommodation, particularly in metropolitan cities such as Mumbai, where officials often undertake long commutes due to limited government housing. She informed that efforts are underway to expedite the government-to-government land acquisition process through the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) for establishing permanent office premises, as several Income Tax offices in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai presently function from rented buildings.

Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Development of Infrastructure Facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts, a sum of Rs. 810 crore has been allocated in the union budget 2026 for judicial infrastructure. In addition, sum of Rs. 1200 crore has been allocated in the union budget 2026 for the eCourts Project Phase-III being implemented for digitisation of courts including necessary training and capacity building programmes. Adequate budgetary provisions are made under these Schemes based on approved outlays and availability of funds. The Government of India, in coordination with the State Government and the Judiciary, has taken several measures to ensure accessible, speedy and effective justice across the country, including in the Tonk–Sawai Madhopur Parliamentary Constituency. Financial assistance is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for strengthening of court infrastructure. Tele-Law services are available through Common Service Centres (CSCs) to provide pre-litigation legal advice. Under the eCourts Project, digital services such as e-Filing, e-Pay, Virtual Courts, video conferencing and the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) have been implemented. Free legal aid is extended through the Legal Services Authorities. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms, including Lok Adalats and mediation, are also being promoted for expeditious resolution of disputes.

Review Meeting on Solid Waste Management on Railway Lands Held in Bengaluru
articles.full_content:
A review meeting on solid waste management on Railway lands and within Greater Bengaluru was held today at the Divisional Railway Office, Bengaluru. The meeting was jointly chaired by Hon'ble Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, and Hon'ble Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, Government of Karnataka, Shri Krishna Byre Gowda.
The meeting discussed the issue of garbage, construction debris and unauthorized dumping of waste on Railway lands. The Ministers reviewed the present situation and emphasized the need for close coordination between the Railways and the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) to keep Railway lands clean.
During the meeting, Railway officials identified several locations where garbage and debris have accumulated due to unauthorized dumping. Shri V. Somanna directed the officials to remove the waste at the earliest and prepare a comprehensive action plan for clearing Railway lands.
The Hon'ble Minister, Shri V. Somanna, stressed that all concerned agencies, including the Greater Bengaluru Authority, Railways, BWSSB, BESCOM and other civic bodies, should work together under a common coordination mechanism to ensure effective waste management. He also noted that the introduction of bio-toilets in trains has brought a significant improvement in railway sanitation.
He directed that strict action, including the imposition of penalties, be taken against those found dumping garbage or debris on railway land.
Shri Krishna Byre Gowda emphasized the need to make Bengaluru free from waste and said that a month-long cleanliness campaign will be launched from August 1, 2026. He also directed officials to remove weeds growing along Railway tracks and said that preventive measures should be taken to stop future dumping.
Both the Ministers instructed officials to identify and close unauthorized access points that are being used for dumping garbage and construction debris onto Railway property.
Officials of the Greater Bengaluru Authority informed the meeting that scientific methods would be adopted for the disposal of waste and assured full cooperation in implementing long-term solutions.
The meeting was attended by Divisional Railway Manager, Bengaluru Division, Shri Ashutosh Kumar Singh; Chief Commissioner, Greater Bengaluru Authority, Shri Maheshwara Rao; Chairperson, BWSSB, Smt. Manjula; Chief Engineer, K-RIDE, Shri Lakshman Singh; and senior officers from South Western Railway and the Greater Bengaluru Authority.
articles.summary: A review meeting on solid waste management on Railway lands and within Greater Bengaluru was held today at the Divisional Railway Office, Bengaluru. The meeting was jointly chaired by Hon'ble Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, and Hon'ble Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, Government of Karnataka, Shri Krishna Byre Gowda.

DPIIT's One District One Product Initiative Promotes 1,244 Unique Products Across 773 Districts
articles.full_content:
PM Ekta Malls and PMFME Scheme Strengthen Market Access for ODOP Products
One District One Product (ODOP) is an initiative by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) with the aim of selecting, branding, and promoting at least one product from each district of the country to enable holistic growth across all regions. The selection of ODOP products is undertaken by the respective State/UT Governments. As of date, 1,244 products have been identified across 773 districts in the country under the ODOP framework.
Several steps have been undertaken to promote and enhance the visibility of the ODOP products includes facilitating participation in domestic and international exhibitions, capacity building initiatives in collaboration with various agencies; e-commerce onboarding drives for Government e-Marketplace (GeM) - ODOP Bazaar.
Under the Scheme for Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI), financial assistance of up to ₹200 crore per State/ Union Territories with legislatures - Delhi, Jammu & Kashmir, and Puducherry is provided through a 50-year interest-free loan for establishment of PM Ekta Malls (Unity Malls) to promote the sale of ODOP, GI, and local handicraft products.
The Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme implemented by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) adopts ODOP approach in food processing sector. It provides 35% credit-linked capital subsidy with maximum for ₹10 lakhs for eligible projects, Seed Capital support to SHG members, Capacity Building through Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) and product-specific training, assistance for Common Infrastructure and Common Incubation Centres, and Branding & Marketing support, including common branding, packaging, quality standardisation and food safety compliance for all the products including ODOP. PMFME Scheme provides support under the Branding & Marketing component @ 50% grant for common branding, packaging, quality standardisation and food safety compliance.
No district-specific financial allocation is made under the ODOP initiative. States/UTs are encouraged to leverage the benefits available under various Central and State Government schemes for the development of ODOP products. These include schemes relating to MSMEs, food processing, skill development, exports, handicrafts, handloom, agriculture, and allied sectors, which provide support for infrastructure development, credit, skill upgradation, quality improvement, branding, market access, and exports.
The PMFME Scheme promotes convergence with other Central initiatives to strengthen both backward and forward linkages. For backward linkages, the Ministry works with the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare to facilitate clustering of Farmers with food processing clusters. For forward linkages, Convergence Committees have been constituted with APEDA and the Department of Fisheries to promote export-oriented value cha

Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) observed Swachhata Pakhwada from 1st to 15th July,2026 across the country.
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 1st to 15th July 2026 with active participation of all Divisions, Attached /Subordinate/ Autonomous Organisations and Field level Offices of the Ministry located across the country.
The Swachhata Pakhwada commenced with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge and a wide cleanliness drive aimed at reinforcing the commitment towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and efficient workplace management.
A comprehensive day-wise action plan was prepared covering activities such as office cleanliness drives, record weeding and review of old files, disposal of obsolete and unserviceable items, digital housekeeping and promotion of e-office practices. Special emphasis was laid on improving office surroundings and enhancing workplace hygiene.
During the fortnight, various Divisions and Offices of the Ministry as well as field offices of MoSPI located across the country organized a wide range of activities including plantation drives, Swachhata awareness campaigns, seminars, workshops, quiz competitions, essay and poster competitions, rallies, shramdaan programmes and community outreach initiatives aimed at promoting public awareness on cleanliness and environmental protection.
The Ministry also undertook initiatives related to reduction of single-use plastic, waste segregation, recycling and sustainable waste management practices in line with the objectives of the Government of India's Swachh Bharat Mission.
As part of the Pakhwada, best practices and innovative initiatives undertaken by various Divisions and Regional Offices were documented and disseminated across the Ministry to encourage wider adoption and institutionalization of successful cleanliness initiatives.
The Swachhata Pakhwada concluded on 15 July 2026 with activities undertaken, sharing of achievements and recognition of significant contributions made by various offices and officials towards strengthening the culture of cleanliness within the Ministry.
The Ministry reaffirms its commitment towards the vision of a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable India and calls upon all officials and stakeholders to actively participate in the Swachhata movement.
"Swachhata is not merely an activity, but a collective responsibility and a way of life."

Indian Railways has adopted a comprehensive mechanism for collection, treatment and disposal of waste generated from trains and railway stations. At stations, twin dustbins have been provided for collection and segregation of waste at source. Waste generated in the trains is collected at regular intervals at nominated waste handling stations. These stations have tie-ups with Urban Local Bodies/Municipal Authorities for proper disposal of waste.

Pursuant to the applicability of new Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, Indian Railways has initiated a series of measures for strengthening solid waste management across its establishments.
The Railway Board has issued Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) on Solid Waste Management covering railway stations, trains, railway colonies, hospitals, workshops, production units and all other railway establishments. SoP provides detailed guidelines regarding segregation, collection, transportation, processing and scientific disposal of waste, monitoring mechanisms and well defined responsibilities at all administrative levels.
Zonal Railways has initiated identification of its units which qualify as bulk waste generators as per SWM Rules, 2026. An “As-is Waste Characterization and Quantification Study” has been planned to assess the existing waste generation across all Indian Railways establishments and trains.
Zonal Railways have also nominated dedicated Nodal Officers to prepare comprehensive action plans for Waste Management, conduct periodic audits, monitor implementation and regularly share compliance reports to Railway Board. Divisions have also been directed to prepare action plans for effective waste management. Dedicated Environment & Housekeeping Management (EnHM) departments have been established at Divisions, Zonal Railways and Railway Board level to monitor and handle waste management related matters.

Study Warns of Growing Water Stress in Uttarakhand's Kosi River Basin Under Climate Change
articles.full_content:
- Research Highlights Rising Temperatures, Reduced Groundwater Recharge, and Increased Drought Risk in the Central Himalaya - According to the study, significant changes are likely to occur in the basin's hydrological cycle during the 21st century
A recent study by researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (IIT Roorkee) and G. B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment (GBPNIHE), Kosi, has warned that climate change could significantly impact long-term water security in Uttarakhand's Kosi River Basin. The findings indicate rising temperatures, declining groundwater recharge, and increasing drought risks that could affect agriculture, drinking water supplies, and fragile Himalayan ecosystems across the Kumaon region.
The study, published in the journal Theoretical and Applied Climatology, was carried out by Dr. B. Das and Dr. S. Sen from IIT Roorkee, along with Dr. Sandipan Mukherjee from GBPNIHE. Using the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) model integrated with projections from five leading global climate models, the researchers assessed the likely impacts of future climate scenarios on the hydrological behaviour of the basin.
The projections point to substantial changes in the basin's hydrological cycle throughout the 21st century, with temperatures expected to rise steadily across all climate scenarios. Peak temperatures in the basin, currently averaging around 38.4°C, could increase to approximately 41.6°C under a moderate-emissions scenario and nearly 43.2°C under a high-emissions scenario by the end of the century. Both maximum and minimum temperatures are projected to rise substantially, intensifying water loss through evaporation and affecting overall water availability.
Dr. I. D. Bhatt, Director, GBPNIHE: " The study highlights a critical shift in the hydrology of Himalayan catchments, where warmer temperatures are expected to intensify evapotranspiration and reduce groundwater replenishment. As mountain communities depend heavily on springs and local water sources, proactive adaptation measures and science-based water management strategies will be essential to enhance resilience against future climate and drought risks." Despite uncertainties in future rainfall patterns, the study suggests that total water yield in the basin may decline by approximately 4–7 percent by 2100. Increased temperatures are expected to raise evapotranspiration by nearly 13 percent, while groundwater recharge may decrease by more than 20 percent. At the same time, surface runoff could increase by about 20 percent, resulting in faster movement of rainwater through the landscape and reduced infiltration into groundwater systems.
Prof. Kamal Kishore Pant, Director, IIT Roorkee: "Climate change poses one of the most significant challenges to water security in mountain ecosystems. Studies such as this provide vital scientific insights for developing evidence-based policies and adaptation strategies that can help safeguard water resource
articles.summary: - Research Highlights Rising Temperatures, Reduced Groundwater Recharge, and Increased Drought Risk in the Central Himalaya - According to the study, significant changes are likely to occur in the basin's hydrological cycle during the 21st century A recent study by researchers from the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (IIT Roorkee) and G. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment (GBPNIHE), Kosi, has warned that climate change could significantly impact long-term water security in Uttarakhand's Kosi River Basin. The findings indicate rising temperatures, declining groundwater recharge, and increasing drought risks that could affect agriculture, drinking water supplies, and fragile Himalayan ecosystems across the Kumaon region.

India's Mine Closure Journey Demonstrates Science Can Transform Environmental Challenges into Development Opportunities: Dr Jitendra Singh India's Scientific Mine Closure Model Can Inspire Sustainable Development Across Sectors: Dr Jitendra Singh Scientific Mine Closure Strengthens India's Journey Towards Net Zero and Sustainable Development: Dr Jitendra Singh
Describing the Mine closure as is a landmark initiative in India's transition towards circular economy, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and Minister of State for the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today said that India is redefining the very idea of mine closure by transforming exhausted mines into new centres of wealth creation, environmental restoration and sustainable livelihoods.
Referring to scientific mine closure as an embodiment of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of innovation-led governance, Dr. Jitendra Singh said a closed mine should no longer be viewed as the end of economic activity but as the beginning of a new development journey that serves both people and the planet.
Dr. Jitendra Singh was addressing the release of "AAROH- Annual Report on Mine Closure", organised by the Ministry of Coal in New Delhi. The event was graced by Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Secretary, Ministry of Coal Vikram Dev Dutt, senior officials of the Ministry, representatives of coal companies, industry leaders and international partners. The programme also witnessed the virtual inauguration of Coal NEER Plants, signing of the Implementation Agreement between the Ministry of Coal and GIZ for technical cooperation on closed coal mines, and Tripartite MoUs for establishing vocational training centres to create sustainable livelihood opportunities in coal-bearing regions.
Calling the initiative a landmark in India's transition towards a circular economy, Dr. Jitendra Singh said scientific mine closure simultaneously advances several national priorities, including waste-to-wealth, resource efficiency, environmental conservation, sustainable land use and community development. "You have closed a coal mine and opened another mine of wealth," he remarked, describing the initiative as a powerful example of how science and technology can unlock fresh economic opportunities from assets that had long been considered exhausted.
The Minister said such transformative thinking has become possible because the present Government encourages innovation instead of remaining confined to conventional approaches. He said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has consistently inspired institutions to challenge established practices and adopt bold, future-oriented solutions capable of delivering long-term national gains. Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman outlines 5Rs of responsive tax governance; Calls for greater tax certainty and reduced litigation at the 167th Income Tax celebrations in New Delhi today
articles.full_content:
The Union Finance Minister reiterates fair, efficient, transparent and taxpayer-centric administration Income-tax Act, 2025 and new rules and forms mark landmark reforms towards simpler and taxpayer-friendly tax system: Revenue Secretary Shri Arvind Shrivastava CBDT Chairman Ravi Agarwal highlights progress in faster return processing, grievance redressal and litigation reduction CBDT advances technology-led tax administration through PAN 2.0, ITBA 2.0, IEC 3.0 and SAKSHAM NUDGE FM Smt. Sitharaman releases six publications highlighting India's growing leadership in international taxation and taxpayer-centric governance
Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated in the 167 th anniversary of Income Tax Day celebrations by Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in New Delhi today.
Shri Arvind Srivastava, Secretary, D/o Revenue; Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT; Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC: Members of CBDT and CBIC and other senior officers and officials of the Department were present on the occasion.
Addressing the 167th Income Tax Day celebrations, Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman emphasised that the role of the Income Tax Department has evolved from tax collection to building a fair, efficient, transparent and taxpayer-centric tax administration. She described the implementation of the Income-tax Act, 2025 as a landmark reform that has simplified the law, reduced compliance costs and strengthened ease of doing business. She also highlighted the enhanced capacity of the e-Filing portal, improved return processing, prompt refunds and significant progress in grievance redressal, while stressing that the Department must move beyond disposal of grievances to analysing recurring issues and preventing them through systemic improvements. She outlined the 5Rs of Responsive Tax Governance - Recognise, Respond, Redress, Reflect and Reform, as guiding principles for taxpayer service, emphasising that honest taxpayers should experience convenience, opportunities to correct bona fide errors and a tax administration that exercises its authority with humility. Stressing that taxpayers are partners in India's development, she called for a continued focus on reducing litigation by strengthening tax certainty.
FM Smt. Sitharaman also underlined the importance of strengthening institutional capacity through modern infrastructure, technology and continuous investment in human capital. She appreciated the progress made in upgrading offices and welfare facilities and called for greater capacity building in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, forensic accounting, international taxation, transfer pricing, digital assets, cybersecurity and leadership development. Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Organises Voluntary Blood Donation Camp
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) organised a Voluntary Blood Donation Camp at Atal Akshay Urja Bhawan, New Delhi, today, reaffirming its commitment to social responsibility and community welfare.
The camp received an encouraging response from officers and staff of the Ministry. A total of 109 officers and staff members voluntarily participated in the blood donation drive, contributing to the success of the event.
The blood donation camp was inaugurated by the Secretary, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Shri Santosh Kumar Sarangi, who lauded the enthusiastic participation of donors. He emphasized that voluntary blood donation is a noble act capable of saving countless lives. Appreciating the spirit of service displayed by the participants, he encouraged everyone to continue supporting such humanitarian initiatives.
A certificate of appreciation was presented to all blood donors in recognition of their selfless contribution.
The Ministry expresses its sincere gratitude to all donors, the organising team, the supporting medical staff for their valuable contribution in making the event a success. The Ministry remains committed to promoting voluntary blood donation and other initiatives that contribute to the health and well-being of society.
"Every Blood Donor is a Hero – Your Donation Can Save Lives."
articles.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) organised a Voluntary Blood Donation Camp at Atal Akshay Urja Bhawan, New Delhi, today, reaffirming its commitment to social responsibility and community welfare. The camp received an encouraging response from officers and staff of the Ministry. A total of 109 officers and staff members voluntarily participated in the blood donation drive, contributing to the success of the event.
